text: Thirty-seven participants (10%) in the intervention group and 62 participants (18%) in the control group developed new-onset MDD throughout the 12-month follow-up, with a hazard ratio of 0.58 (95% confidence interval 0.38-0.87; p = 0.008).

The app-based CBT-I group has higher remission rates of insomnia disorder than the controls at post-intervention (52% versus 28%; relative risk 1.83 [1.49-2.24]; p < 0.001) and throughout 12-month follow-up.

Between September 9, 2019, and November 25, 2022, 708 participants (407 females [57%]; mean age, 22.1 years [SD = 1.9]) were randomly allocated to app-based CBT-I group (n = 354) or app-based HE group (n = 354).

abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the effectiveness of FA dCBT-I across 29 randomized controlled trials (RCTs) involving 9475 participants.
Subgroup analyses indicated that FA dCBT-I had a significant impact when contrasted with most control groups but was less effective than therapist-assisted CBT-I.
Meta-regression revealed that control group type moderated outcomes, whereas completion rate did not.

full_text.Methods, Search strategy: We searched the PubMed, CENTRAL, Embase and PsycINFO databases for studies published up to March 31, 2024.
full_text.Methods, registration: The protocol for this review was registered with the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO) (CRD42024526617).
full_text.Methods, Study selection: After removing duplicates, two authors (J.W.H. and G.E.L) independently screened the titles and abstracts based on the inclusion and exclusion criteria.
full_text.Methods, Study selection (2): Disagreements were resolved by consensus, or through discussion with a third reviewer (J.Y.K) when consensus could not be reached.
full_text.Methods, Data extraction: Two authors (J.W.H and G.E.L) independently extracted data from the included studies
full_text.Results, Study flow: A total of 3101 articles were identified from four databases, and 129 articles remained after the deduplication and screening process. A total of 29 studies were included after the full text review.
full_text.Results, Risk of bias: Figure 2 displays the results of the risk of bias assessment using the RoB 2.0 tool. Three studies were judged to have a low risk of bias, 19 had some concerns, and 7 were considered high risk.
full_text.Results, insomnia severity: Statistical heterogeneity across studies for effect sizes was considerable (Fig. 3 ; I 2 = 91%; Q = 330.81; df = 31; p < 0.001).
full_text.Results, Publication bias: The result of Egger's test revealed no statistically significant publication bias (t = 1.34, df = 30, p = 0.19).
